title: US-Iran Conflict: US Reinstates Maritime Blockade on Iran; Strikes Iranian Submarine Centre Using Sea Drones
summary: The United States reinstated a maritime blockade on Iran amid escalating military conflict, with US forces conducting strikes on Iran including, for the first time, an attack on an Iranian submarine centre using sea drones. Iran retaliated by targeting vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and hitting Gulf nations. President Trump also demanded a 20% fee for US protection of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran called excessive.
exam_angle: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global oil chokepoint; US-Iran tensions directly impact India's energy security, trade routes, and crude oil imports. Relevant for GS Paper 2 (International Relations) and GS Paper 3 (Energy Security).
key_facts: US reinstated maritime blockade on Iran and struck Iranian submarine centre using sea drones
Strait of Hormuz: ~20% of global oil trade passes through it; critical for India's energy imports
Trump demanded 20% fee for US protection of shipping in Hormuz
Iran retaliated by targeting vessels in the Strait of Hormuz

title: India's Trade Deficit Widens to Five-Month High of $30.43 Billion in June 2026 Amid Hormuz Disruptions
summary: India's merchandise trade deficit widened to a five-month high of $30.43 billion in June 2026, a jump of approximately 430% year-on-year, driven by surging imports of oil, gold, and electronics amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. The US-Iran conflict has added risk to India's import-heavy trade outlook. Weak exports also contributed to the widening deficit.
exam_angle: India's trade deficit trends are key data points for GS Paper 3 (Economy); the Hormuz disruption illustrates the vulnerability of India's import-dependent economy to geopolitical shocks.
key_facts: Trade deficit: $30.43 billion in June 2026 (five-month high)
Deficit jumped ~430% year-on-year in June 2026
Key drivers: surging oil, gold, and electronics imports
Hormuz disruptions cited as a major risk factor for India's trade outlook

title: India-US Trade Deal Framework 'Ready'; Agriculture and Comparative Advantage Still Under Negotiation
summary: India's Commerce Secretary stated that the framework for an India-US bilateral trade deal is ready but certain aspects, particularly comparative advantage and agriculture, are still being worked out. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal rejected reports that India was holding out on the deal. The US Ambassador also denied reports that India had rejected a quick deal, calling them 'fake news'.
exam_angle: India-US trade negotiations are a recurring theme in GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy); key issues include tariffs, agriculture market access, and intellectual property — all potential exam topics.
key_facts: India-US trade deal framework described as 'ready' by Commerce Secretary
India firm on not ceding ground on agriculture in trade talks
Comparative advantage clauses still under negotiation
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal denied India is holding back on the deal

title: Ladakh to Get UT-Level Governance Body and Hill Councils for All Seven Districts Under Customised Article 371 Framework
summary: The Central Government announced that Ladakh will receive a Union Territory-level governance body along with Autonomous Hill Councils extended to all seven districts, under a framework described as a 'customised Article 371 arrangement'. Currently, hill councils exist only in Leh and Kargil districts. Ladakh also created 17 new tehsils to improve administrative access for citizens.
exam_angle: This is directly relevant to GS Paper 2 (Polity) — Article 371 special provisions, the status of Ladakh as a UT without legislature (post-Article 370 abrogation), and the demand for statehood/legislature by Ladakh.
key_facts: Ladakh to get a UT-level governance body and hill councils in all 7 districts
Framework described as 'customised Article 371 arrangement'
Currently hill councils exist only in Leh and Kargil districts
17 new tehsils created in Ladakh to improve administrative access

title: Supreme Court Seeks Centre's New Aviation Rules to Regulate Airfare Volatility Within Two Weeks
summary: The Supreme Court directed the Central Government to place on record new aviation rules aimed at regulating volatile airfares within two weeks, accepting them in a sealed cover. The court expressed concern over 'unpredictable fluctuations' in domestic airfares. The Ministry of Civil Aviation is expected to submit the regulatory framework being devised.
exam_angle: Supreme Court interventions in economic regulation are relevant for GS Paper 2 (Polity/Judiciary); also connects to consumer protection rights under Article 21 and the regulatory role of DGCA.
key_facts: Supreme Court asked Centre to submit new aviation airfare regulation rules within 2 weeks
Rules to be submitted in sealed cover
Issue: 'unpredictable fluctuations' in domestic airfares
Regulatory body for civil aviation: DGCA (Directorate General of Civil Aviation)

title: UK Bans Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Links IRGC-Backed Group to Attacks on Jewish Community
summary: The United Kingdom formally banned Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), designating it as a terrorist organisation and holding an IRGC-backed group responsible for attacks on the Jewish community in the UK. The move aligns the UK with the US and EU positions on the IRGC. The ban makes membership in or support of the IRGC a criminal offence in the UK.
exam_angle: IRGC proscription is significant for GS Paper 2 (IR) — it reflects the broader Western response to Iran's regional activities and has implications for multilateral sanctions regimes.
key_facts: UK formally banned Iran's IRGC, designating it a terrorist organisation
IRGC-backed group linked to attacks on UK's Jewish community
Membership or support of IRGC now a criminal offence in the UK
US has designated IRGC as a Foreign Terrorist Organization since 2019

title: PM Modi to Launch India's First Hydrogen-Powered Train on July 17 During Haryana Visit
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to launch India's first hydrogen-powered train during his visit to Haryana on July 17, 2026. The train represents a significant step in India's green hydrogen mission and railway decarbonisation efforts. Indian Railways has been piloting hydrogen fuel cell technology as part of its net-zero 2030 target.
exam_angle: India's first hydrogen-powered train connects to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech / Environment) — Green Hydrogen Mission, railway decarbonisation, and India's net-zero targets are high-priority exam topics.
key_facts: India's first hydrogen-powered train to be launched by PM Modi on July 17, 2026
Launch location: Haryana
Connects to India's National Green Hydrogen Mission
Indian Railways' target: Net Zero Carbon Emissions by 2030

title: Aditya Birla Group to Acquire Shell's Sprng Energy for $1.8 Billion in Major Renewables Deal
summary: Aditya Birla Group announced the acquisition of Sprng Energy, Shell's India-based renewable energy arm, for approximately $1.8 billion (around ₹17,200 crore). Sprng Energy has a significant portfolio of solar and wind energy assets in India. The deal marks one of the largest renewable energy acquisitions in India and strengthens Aditya Birla Group's position in the clean energy sector.
exam_angle: Large-scale renewable energy M&A activity is relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy/Environment) — highlights private sector role in India's energy transition and the 500 GW non-fossil fuel target by 2030.
key_facts: Aditya Birla Group acquires Sprng Energy from Shell for $1.8 billion (~₹17,200 crore)
Sprng Energy is Shell's India-based renewable energy arm
One of the largest renewable energy acquisitions in India
Connects to India's target of 500 GW renewable energy capacity by 2030

title: MeitY Releases 2nd Edition of Digital Threat Report 2025-26 for India's BFSI Sector
summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) released the second edition of the Digital Threat Report 2025-26 for India's Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) sector, in collaboration with SISA. The report flagged that six of seven cyber threats identified in the previous year have now become operational. The BFSI sector is identified as the most targeted sector for cyberattacks in India.
exam_angle: Cybersecurity reports from MeitY are relevant for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Internal Security); the BFSI sector's cyber vulnerability connects to critical infrastructure protection — a common exam theme.
key_facts: Report: MeitY's Digital Threat Report 2025-26, 2nd edition for India's BFSI sector
Released in collaboration with SISA
6 of 7 cyber threats flagged last year are now operational
BFSI sector is India's most targeted sector for cyberattacks

title: Tahir Hussain Convicted for Murder of IB Officer Ankit Sharma During 2020 Delhi Riots
summary: Former AAP leader Tahir Hussain has been convicted by a Delhi court for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the February 2020 Northeast Delhi riots. Hussain was accused of orchestrating mob violence from his residence. The case was one of the most prominent arising from the Delhi riots, which resulted in over 50 deaths.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (Polity/Governance) and GS Paper 3 (Internal Security) — the Delhi riots case involved communal violence, law enforcement, and the role of elected representatives in incitement.
key_facts: Tahir Hussain (former AAP leader) convicted for murder of IB officer Ankit Sharma
Crime took place during February 2020 Northeast Delhi riots
Delhi riots resulted in 53+ deaths
Hussain was arrested in 2020; case investigated by Delhi Police Special Cell

title: Jharkhand Police Arrest Top Maoist Leader Ravindra Ganjhu in Major Anti-Naxal Operation
summary: Jharkhand Police arrested top Maoist leader Ravindra Ganjhu in a major anti-Naxal breakthrough. Ganjhu is described as a senior commander in the CPI (Maoist) organisation. The arrest is seen as a significant blow to Left Wing Extremism (LWE) activities in Jharkhand, one of the most affected states in India's Red Corridor.
exam_angle: Left Wing Extremism (Naxalism) is a key internal security topic for GS Paper 3; arrests of top leadership are used by the government to showcase progress in its anti-Naxal strategy.
key_facts: Arrested: Ravindra Ganjhu, top Maoist/CPI(Maoist) leader
Arrested by: Jharkhand Police
Jharkhand is part of India's LWE-affected 'Red Corridor'
Government aims to eliminate LWE by 2026 under its security grid approach

title: Dhruva Space Secures First Investment from India's Antariksh Venture Fund
summary: Hyderabad-based Dhruva Space has secured the first investment from India's Antariksh Venture Fund, a government-backed fund-of-funds established to promote the private space ecosystem. This marks the inaugural deployment of the Antariksh Fund, which was set up under the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) framework. Dhruva Space is a leading private space startup in India focused on satellite integration and launch services.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech) — India's space sector reforms including IN-SPACe, the Antariksh Fund, and the role of private players like Dhruva Space are frequently examined topics.
key_facts: Dhruva Space: first company to receive investment from India's Antariksh Venture Fund
Antariksh Fund: government-backed fund-of-funds for private space sector under IN-SPACe
Dhruva Space is based in Hyderabad; focuses on satellite integration and launch services
IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre) regulates and promotes private space activity in India

title: DRI Busts Multiple Wildlife Trafficking Networks Across India
summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) dismantled several wildlife trafficking networks operating across India in a coordinated enforcement operation. The operations resulted in seizures of protected wildlife species and arrests of key traffickers. Wildlife trafficking is a major concern under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 and CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species).
exam_angle: Wildlife crime enforcement is relevant for GS Paper 3 (Environment); DRI's role, CITES obligations, and India's legal framework under the Wildlife Protection Act are standard exam topics.
key_facts: Agency: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) busted multiple wildlife trafficking networks
Key legislation: Wildlife Protection Act, 1972
India is a signatory to CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species)
Wildlife trafficking is a Schedule 1 offence under the Wildlife Protection Act

title: Ukraine and Nine Nations Form Coalition Against Ballistic Missiles to Protect Europe
summary: Ukraine and nine other countries have formed a multilateral coalition aimed at countering ballistic missile threats to European security. The coalition focuses on air defence sharing, intelligence cooperation, and joint procurement of missile defence systems. This development comes amid ongoing Russian missile strikes on Ukraine and growing concern about missile proliferation in Europe.
exam_angle: Multilateral security coalitions are relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR) — NATO, collective security mechanisms, and European security architecture are recurring themes in UPSC.
key_facts: Ukraine + 9 nations formed a coalition against ballistic missile threats in Europe
Focus areas: air defence sharing, intelligence cooperation, joint missile defence procurement
Context: Ongoing Russia-Ukraine war with sustained Russian ballistic missile attacks
Connects to debates on collective security, NATO Article 5, and European defence architecture

title: Trump Moves to Dismantle International Criminal Court, Calling It 'Intolerable Threat to US Sovereignty'
summary: US President Donald Trump announced moves to dismantle the International Criminal Court (ICC), describing it as an 'intolerable threat to US sovereignty.' The US has previously withdrawn from ICC jurisdiction and sanctioned ICC officials. The ICC, based in The Hague, operates under the Rome Statute and has jurisdiction over genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and crimes of aggression.
exam_angle: The ICC and the Rome Statute are standard GS Paper 2 (IR) topics; US non-membership in the ICC and its opposition to the court is a key point for international institutions questions.
key_facts: ICC (International Criminal Court) established under Rome Statute, 1998; operational from 2002
Headquartered in The Hague, Netherlands
USA has never ratified the Rome Statute and is not an ICC member
ICC has jurisdiction over genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and crimes of aggression

title: Bharat Tex 2026: India Prepares to Host World's Largest Global Textiles Expo
summary: India is preparing to host Bharat Tex 2026, described as the world's largest global textiles expo. Union Minister of Textiles Giriraj Singh also visited 'Indie Haat 2026' at the National Crafts Museum, New Delhi, and the 'Weave the Future 4.0' exhibition, highlighting India's rich craft traditions. Bharat Tex is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Textiles to showcase India's textile ecosystem globally.
exam_angle: Bharat Tex and India's textiles export promotion are relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy) — the textile sector is one of India's largest employment generators and a key export sector.
key_facts: Bharat Tex 2026: described as world's largest global textiles expo
Organised by: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
Union Textiles Minister: Giriraj Singh
India's textile sector is 2nd largest employment generator after agriculture

title: Poland Acknowledges PM Modi's Key Diplomatic Role in Russia-Ukraine Conflict
summary: A top Polish official stated that 'Putin pays attention to what PM Modi says,' acknowledging India's significant diplomatic influence in mediating or influencing the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Poland, a frontline NATO state, signalled appreciation for India's engagement with Russia as a potential channel for peace. PM Modi had previously visited both Moscow and Kyiv, urging dialogue.
exam_angle: India's strategic autonomy, its role in the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and PM Modi's diplomatic outreach are high-priority GS Paper 2 (IR) topics; India's position as a voice of the Global South is also relevant.
key_facts: Polish official: 'Putin pays attention to what PM Modi says'
PM Modi has visited both Moscow (July 2024) and Kyiv (August 2024)
India has maintained strategic autonomy — not joining Western sanctions on Russia
India is a major importer of Russian oil since 2022, with discounted crude

title: Oil Companies Plan to Expand Sales of 10-kg LPG Cylinders
summary: State-owned oil companies are planning to expand the sales network for 10-kg LPG cylinders, aimed at offering a more affordable and accessible option compared to the standard 14.2-kg domestic cylinder. The initiative is targeted at lower-income households and small commercial users. The move is expected to complement schemes like PM Ujjwala Yojana by improving LPG penetration.
exam_angle: LPG distribution policy connects to GS Paper 2 (Government Schemes) — PM Ujjwala Yojana, LPG subsidies, and clean cooking fuel access are standard exam topics.
key_facts: Oil PSUs plan expansion of 10-kg LPG cylinder sales across India
10-kg cylinder is more affordable than standard 14.2-kg domestic cylinder
Relevant government scheme: PM Ujjwala Yojana (free LPG connections to BPL households)
India is the 2nd largest LPG consumer in the world
